title: People Treated Stuffed Animals Like Stocks
description:
In the late 1990s, people were taking out loans and draining savings to buy stuffed toys as investments. It's now studied as a textbook speculative bubble.

Educational content, not financial advice.

#shorts #financefacts #economics

scenes.text: In the late 1990s, people were treating stuffed animals like they were stocks.
Beanie Babies, silly little bean-filled toys, started selling for hundreds or even thousands of dollars each.
Retired designs were traded like collectibles, with price guides and secondary markets built entirely around them.
Some people took out loans, or drained retirement savings, betting a certain Beanie Baby would keep going up in value forever.
Then demand collapsed almost overnight, and most of those investments became worthless plush toys again.
It's now studied as one of the clearest examples of a pure speculative bubble that had nothing to do with the actual product.
